learningObjectives.title: Arguments for the existence of God: the design (teleological) argument
Arguments for the existence of God: the cosmological argument
The problem of evil and suffering

questions.q: Which thinker is famous for using the analogy of finding a watch to argue that the universe has a designer?
questions.explain: William Paley argued that just as a watch implies a watchmaker, the ordered universe implies a divine designer.

questions.q: In Paley's argument, the intricate watch found on a heath is used as a comparison for what?
options: The complexity and order of the natural world
The suffering caused by natural disasters
The absence of God in nature
questions.explain: Paley claimed the design seen in a watch is mirrored by the order and purpose found throughout nature.

questions.q: Why is Charles Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection seen as a challenge to the design argument?
options: It explains apparent design as the result of natural processes rather than a designer
It proves that God created every species separately
It shows the universe had no beginning
It supports the idea of a first cause
questions.explain: Evolution offers a natural explanation for the appearance of design, removing the need for a divine designer.

questions.q: A student argues that because the human eye is so complex and perfectly suited to seeing, it must have been designed by God. Which argument is this an example of?
questions.explain: Pointing to complexity and purpose in nature as evidence of a designer is the design argument.

questions.q: The cosmological argument concludes that God must exist as the:
questions.explain: The cosmological argument reasons that the universe must have an uncaused first cause, identified as God.

questions.q: Which Christian thinker set out arguments for God's existence known as the 'Five Ways'?
questions.explain: Thomas Aquinas presented his Five Ways, including cosmological arguments from motion, cause and contingency.

questions.q: Which idea best summarises the reasoning behind the cosmological argument?
options: Everything that exists has a cause, so the universe must have a first cause
The complexity of nature proves a designer
Personal experiences of God prove he exists
questions.explain: The cosmological argument moves from cause and effect in the universe to the need for an uncaused first cause.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common objection to the cosmological argument?
options: If everything needs a cause, then what caused God?
The universe is too ordered to be random
Evil proves the universe was designed
questions.explain: Critics argue that if everything requires a cause, God should too, which undermines the idea of an uncaused first cause.

questions.q: Evil and suffering caused deliberately by human beings, such as murder or theft, is known as:
questions.explain: Moral evil is suffering brought about by the free choices and actions of human beings.

questions.q: Suffering caused by natural events such as earthquakes, floods and disease is known as:
questions.explain: Natural evil is suffering that results from the natural world rather than human action.

questions.q: The problem of evil questions how evil can exist if God is both:
questions.explain: The problem is that an all-powerful, all-loving God would seem both able and willing to prevent evil, yet evil exists.

questions.q: How does the 'free will defence' respond to the problem of evil?
options: God gave humans free will, and evil is the result of humans misusing it
God does not exist because evil exists
Evil is an illusion that does not really happen
God causes evil to punish sinners
questions.explain: The free will defence argues that genuine free will makes moral evil possible, but is a greater good than forced obedience.

questions.q: Which of the following is a Christian response to suffering?
options: Suffering can be a test of faith and an opportunity for spiritual growth
Suffering proves that God is not all-powerful
Suffering shows the universe has no purpose
Suffering is caused only by natural laws with no meaning
questions.explain: Many Christians believe suffering can test and strengthen faith, following the example of Jesus's own suffering.

questions.q: A believer describes the suffering caused by a tsunami that no human being brought about. This is an example of:
questions.explain: A tsunami is a natural event, so the suffering it causes is classed as natural evil.

questions.q: The feeling of awe and wonder in the presence of a holy or divine power is often called:
questions.explain: The numinous describes the sense of awe, mystery and wonder felt in the presence of God.

questions.q: What is the difference between general revelation and special revelation?
options: General revelation is available to everyone through nature and conscience, while special revelation is a direct experience given to particular people
General revelation only happens in dreams, while special revelation happens in churches
General revelation is false, while special revelation is true
There is no difference between the two terms
questions.explain: General revelation is indirect and open to all, whereas special revelation is a direct, personal disclosure of God.

questions.q: Which statement best describes what religious believers usually mean by a miracle?
options: An event that breaks the laws of nature and is attributed to God
Any lucky or fortunate everyday event
A scientific discovery about the universe
A natural disaster that causes suffering
questions.explain: A miracle is generally understood as an act of God that goes beyond or breaks the normal laws of nature.

questions.q: A conversion experience is best described as:
options: A religious experience that leads a person to change their beliefs and commit to a faith
A scientific proof that God exists
A natural disaster sent as a punishment
A logical argument for a first cause
questions.explain: A conversion experience is a religious experience that transforms a person's beliefs and commitment to God.

questions.q: After recovering from a serious illness, a woman feels an overwhelming sense of a loving presence and dedicates the rest of her life to God. This is best described as:
questions.explain: A direct experience of God that changes someone's life and commitment is a religious conversion experience.

questions.q: In a debate, a student says: 'Everything must have been started off by something, and that first something is God.' Which argument is the student using?
questions.explain: Arguing that the universe needs a first cause, identified as God, is the cosmological argument.
